# core/chacha20poly1305.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/chacha20poly1305.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Authenticated encryption with ChaCha20 and
Poly1305 (RFC 8439 section 2.8).

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, a sealed message
is 16 bytes longer than its plaintext, and `aead_open` returns `Some` only
after the tag has been compared in full. Not proved: that the output is
RFC 8439's (the tests check its vectors, a tampered byte in every position,
and a differential run against a reference), or that the code is constant
time (the tag comparison folds all 16 bytes without an early exit).

A nonce must never be used twice with one key.

`import "core/chacha20poly1305.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/chacha20.bastio](core-chacha20.md), [core/poly1305.bastio](core-poly1305.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`aead_seal`](#aead_seal) | Encrypts `plain` under the 32-byte `key` and 12-byte `nonce`, and authenticates it together with `aad` (which stays in the clear). |
| [`aead_open`](#aead_open) | Checks the tag at the end of `sealed` and, if it is right, decrypts. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `aead_seal`

```bastio
fn aead_seal(key: &Bytes, nonce: &Bytes, aad: &Bytes, plain: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(key) == 32 && blen(nonce) == 12 && blen(plain) < 274877906944
  ensures blen(result) == blen(plain) + 16
```

Encrypts `plain` under the 32-byte `key` and 12-byte `nonce`, and
authenticates it together with `aad` (which stays in the clear): the
ciphertext followed by a 16-byte tag.

Example:

```bastio
let mut key = balloc(32);
let mut i = 0;
while i < 32 invariant i <= 32 && blen(key) == 32 { bset(&mut key, i, cast[u8](i + 128)); i = i + 1; }
let nonce = balloc(12);
let aad = bfrom("header");
let plain = bfrom("attack at dawn");
let sealed = aead_seal(key, nonce, aad, plain);
let n = blen(sealed);
let mut ok = false;
match aead_open(key, nonce, aad, sealed) {
  Option::Some(p) => { ok = bytes_eq(p, plain); bfree(p); },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(sealed);
bfree(plain);
bfree(aad);
bfree(nonce);
bfree(key);
if n != 30 || !ok { return 1; }
```

### `aead_open`

```bastio
fn aead_open(key: &Bytes, nonce: &Bytes, aad: &Bytes, sealed: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(key) == 32 && blen(nonce) == 12 && blen(sealed) < 274877906944
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) + 16 == blen(sealed)
```

Checks the tag at the end of `sealed` and, if it is right, decrypts: the
plaintext. `None` for a message shorter than a tag, or one whose tag, data
or `aad` was changed.

Example:

```bastio
let mut key = balloc(32);
let nonce = balloc(12);
let aad = balloc(0);
let plain = bfrom("x");
let mut sealed = aead_seal(key, nonce, aad, plain);
bset(&mut sealed, 0, bget(sealed, 0) ^ 1);     // flip a bit
let mut refused = true;
match aead_open(key, nonce, aad, sealed) {
  Option::Some(p) => { refused = false; bfree(p); },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(sealed);
bfree(plain);
bfree(aad);
bfree(nonce);
bfree(key);
if !refused { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `aead_pad16`

```bastio
fn aead_pad16(t: &mut Vec[u8])
```

Internal: pads the text `t` with zeros to a multiple of 16 bytes.

### `aead_push_le64`

```bastio
fn aead_push_le64(t: &mut Vec[u8], x: u64)
```

Internal: appends `x` as 8 little-endian bytes.

### `aead_tag`

```bastio
fn aead_tag(key: &Bytes, nonce: &Bytes, aad: &Bytes, ct: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(key) == 32 && blen(nonce) == 12
  ensures blen(result) == 16
```

Internal: the Poly1305 tag over `aad`, `ct`, padded, and both lengths,
under the one-time key from block 0 of the cipher.
